title: Transition in the Negative-Answer State
statement: Let $F$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine, let $\mathrm{inp}$ be an optional Boolean input symbol, and let $w$ assign a possibly blank Boolean symbol to each of the constructed oracle machine's $k+1$ work tapes. In its negative-answer state, the constructed machine's transition is the action that emits false, leaves the input and work tapes unmoved and unwritten, and halts.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a finite-state binary Turing machine
$\mathrm{inp}$ is an optional Boolean input symbol
$w$ gives an optional Boolean symbol for each of the $k+1$ work tapes
